H&P – Super Detailed Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
25-year-old woman with 2-month history of escalating work-related anxiety, insomnia, and episodic morning palpitations; likely adjustment disorder/early generalized anxiety, plans for talking therapy and baseline blood tests arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Really anxious over the past few months,” daily dread of leaving the house for work.  
• Onset/Timeline: Began ≈2 months ago after starting a new, highly stressful job in a fashion-retail head-office; progressively worsening.  
• Symptoms:  
  – Excessive worry about work performance; fear of being late.  
  – Insomnia: bedtime 22:00–23:00, sleep latency “hours,” total sleep ≈3–4 h, shallow; wakes before alarm with racing heart.  
  – Palpitations: irregular rapid heartbeat lasting minutes (up to 10 min), mainly on waking; one episode felt like impending heart attack; no true chest pain, syncope, or prior cardiac history.  
  – Low daytime energy, anhedonia (running, tennis, socialising no longer enjoyable).  
  – Social withdrawal/avoidance of friends; difficulty engaging in hobbies.  
  – Low mood “pretty much down,” but denies suicidal ideation or self-harm thoughts.  
• Exacerbating factors: Thoughts of work, mornings, public transport (tube).  
• Relieving factors: None identified.  
• Review of systems (pertinent):  
  – Appetite largely unchanged (slightly more chocolate); no weight change reported.  
  – No tremor, heat intolerance, bowel change, or other hyperthyroid symptoms elicited.  
  – No prior panic attacks; no previous similar anxiety episodes.  

Past Medical History:
• No chronic medical conditions reported.  
• No current medications reported.  
• Allergies: not discussed.  

Social History:
• Lives with parents.  
• Occupation: Fashion-retail head-office; new position; reports hostile manager and high stress.  
• Alcohol: Binge pattern—exceeds limits on Fri/Sat nights when out; occasional glass of wine during week; exact units not quantified.  
• Tobacco: Occasional smoker.  
• Recreational drugs: Denies.  

Family History:
• Mother with history of depression.  
• No family cardiac disorders mentioned.  

Physical Examination:
(Teleconsultation; no vitals or exam performed.)

Investigations:
• Planned: “Couple of basic blood tests” (details not specified; likely FBC, TSH, metabolic panel per usual practice) to evaluate palpitations/underlying contributors.  
• No prior investigations available.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Work-related anxiety (probable Adjustment Disorder vs evolving Generalized Anxiety Disorder):
  • Assessment: Temporal link to new job; pervasive worry, somatic tension, insomnia, functional impact.  
  • Plan:  
    – Provide NHS self-referral link for talking therapy (CBT).  
    – Supply reputable online anxiety-management resources.  
    – Advise patient to re-contact GP if symptoms escalate or interfere with ability to work/cope; consider pharmacotherapy at that stage.

Issue 2 – Insomnia secondary to anxiety:
  • Plan:  
    – Written advice on sleep hygiene (bedtime routine, screen avoidance, caffeine/alcohol moderation, regular exercise when feasible).  
    – Address underlying anxiety (as above).

Issue 3 – Palpitations:
  • Assessment: Most likely anxiety-related; differential includes arrhythmia, thyroid dysfunction, anaemia.  
  • Plan:  
    – Order baseline labs (FBC, TSH, U&Es, HbA1c, ± ferritin) – patient to book via support line.  
    – Arrange GP follow-up one week after tests to review results and reconsider need for further cardiac work-up if abnormal findings or persistent palpitations.

General/Lifestyle:
  • Encourage gradual return to physical activity (running, tennis) as tolerated.  
  • Discuss reducing binge alcohol intake; offer brief advice resources.  
  • Smoking: encourage cessation; offer NHS stop-smoking support information.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Adjustment disorder with anxiety / early Generalized Anxiety Disorder – High likelihood: clear onset after occupational stressor, chronic worry, somatic symptoms.  
2. Major depressive disorder with anxious distress – Moderate likelihood: low mood, anhedonia, fatigue, family history; suicidality absent.  
3. Hyperthyroidism – Low-moderate likelihood: palpitations and insomnia could mimic anxiety; to be screened with TSH; absence of classic hyperthyroid signs lowers probability.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing but expected: allergies and regular medication list not obtained; no vitals or physical exam (televisit).  
• Conflicts: none noted between transcript and DDx.  
• Transcript quality: clear; minor repetition, no significant inaudible sections.
